title: whyitbroke report
description: What `whyitbroke --json` prints: one report per run. Version 1 only ever gains fields, and a field it has keeps its meaning, so an object here may carry fields this schema does not list yet.

tool.description: The tool whose output this is, named by the parser that read it. null when nothing in the output could be read.

summary.description: The run's tally as the tool stated it, or as whyitbroke counted it where the tool states none.

guessed.description: No parser recognised the tool, and the failures are the generic reader's best guess.

wrappers.description: What was taken off the output before it could be read, outermost first: the name of a known shape (`docker`, `jenkins`, `kubectl logs`), or the literal prefix removed from every line (`api:test: `).

clusters.description: `failures` grouped by likely cause. Every failure is a member of exactly one entry. null with `--no-cluster`.

others.description: Failures that other tools printed into the same output, one entry per tool. null when there were none.

exitCode.description: whyitbroke's own exit code: the wrapped command's, 0 for piped input it processed, 127 for a command that could not be started.

inputMode.description: Whether whyitbroke ran the command itself or read piped input.

commandExitCode.description: The wrapped command's exit code. null for piped input, whose upstream status is unknown, and for a command that could not be started.

status.description: What the exit status says by itself, when it says anything. A signal is a fact the operating system reported; an exit code means something only by a shell's convention, and only for a command whyitbroke ran. null when the number says nothing.

fallback.description: Set when the command failed, or input was piped, and nothing in the output could be read.

truncated.description: The output was larger than `--max-bytes`, and parts of it were not kept.

error.description: Why the command could not be started.

since.description: With `--since-last`: how this run's causes compare with the last tracked run of the same command, for the same tool, in the same directory.

failures.description: What the tool reported. Empty does not mean the command succeeded: check `commandExitCode`.

severity.description: How the tool classed it. A warning is never reported as a failure.

title.description: What the failure is called: its `code`, `subject` or `label`, or the tool's own name for it. Can be empty.

message.description: What the tool said about it, one or more lines.

subject.description: The name of what failed: a test, a method.

label.description: A constant the tool prints for a class of failure: `compile error`.

file.description: The file, as the tool named it.

col.description: The column in `line`, counting from 1, in the tool's own unit: bytes for some tools, UTF-16 code units or characters for others. Most count a tab as one column. On a line of plain ASCII with no tabs, every unit agrees.

stmt.description: The source line the tool quoted.

trace.description: The stack frames kept, in the order the tool printed them. The first is where the failure happened.

hiddenFrames.description: How many frames were left out of `trace` as the internals of a runtime or a tool.

evidence.description: The lines of the output this failure was read from, in order and apart. A line ends at a line feed, and the lines count from 1 in the output as it arrived: all of a pipe's input, or everything a command wrote to stdout and stderr. When the capture was cut short, what was left out still counts, so the numbers are the output's and not the capture's.

end.description: The last line, which is `start` or after it.

id.description: A fingerprint of what the members share. For an entry that is not reported it also includes the member's position.

signature.description: What the members have in common, with the parts that vary between them abstracted away.

members.description: Indices into the `failures` array this entry groups.

exemplar.description: The member shown for the whole group: one of `members`.

reported.description: Whether this is claimed as one likely cause. A failure whose cause is not confidently shared is its own entry, not reported.

count.description: How many failures are listed for it.

summary.description: The tool's tally, present only when every failure it reported is listed here.

clusters.description: This tool's `failures` grouped by likely cause, as for the report's own.

failures.description: What it reported that the report's own tool did not.

compared.description: Whether there was a previous run to compare with.

reason.description: Why nothing was compared. `unidentified-pipe`: the log was piped in and not named with --id, so there is nothing to tell it from any other pipeline run in the same directory.

fresh.description: The causes that were not in the previous run.

gone.description: How many of the previous run's causes this run no longer reports. null when this run cannot say, as `goneWithheld` explains.

ranAt.description: When the previous run was recorded, as an ISO 8601 instant.

recorded.description: Whether this run was saved for the next one to compare with. A truncated run, or a command that could not be started, never is.

migrated.description: The previous run was saved by an older version of whyitbroke and compared through its identifiers.

signal.description: The signal that killed the command, as the operating system names it. null when it exited on its own.

code.description: The exit code this was read from - 128 plus the signal's number, where a signal ended it.

says.description: What that means, in a sentence. Where a second sentence names a usual cause it is a guess, and says so.

reason.description: Why there is nothing to report.

message.description: The same explanation, as a sentence.

rawOutput.description: What was captured, which can be empty. Check `truncated` before treating it as complete.
